query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor aluminum addition (~5 at.%) to equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr will promote the in situ formation of a thin, adherent alumina (Al2O3) scale during high‐temperature exposure, thereby significantly improving its oxygen resistance without degrading its useful mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr with demonstrated room-temperature tensile ductility (8–16%) and high-temperature yield strength (163–530 MPa at 1000 °C) but inadequate oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Alloy modification by partially substituting approximately 5 at.% of one of the refractory species with aluminum.
generation.conditions: Exposure in air at temperatures between 800 °C and 1000 °C for 5 hours, under similar strain rate and mechanical loading conditions as previously characterized.
generation.structural_mediator: Development of a continuous, adherent alumina (Al2O3) surface scale on the alloy.
generation.mechanism: The added aluminum preferentially oxidizes at the surface, forming a protective Al2O3 layer that retards further oxygen ingress and bulk oxidation while preserving the underlying microstructure and mechanical performance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, the Al-modified alloy will show significantly lower oxygen uptake and reduced pesting, with mechanical properties (ductility and high-temperature strength) remaining within an acceptable performance window.
generation.baseline: Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits inadequate oxygen resistance under high-temperature air exposure despite its favorable mechanical properties.
generation.boundary: Effectiveness is anticipated for air exposures of approximately 5 hours at 800–1000 °C and under tensile loading conditions similar to those used in existing performance evaluations; outside these conditions, the protective scale’s formation or stability may vary.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal aluminum content and its potential impact on other phase equilibria or long-term mechanical stability are not fully defined and may require further optimization to avoid possible embrittlement or undesirable phase formation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: (1) the baseline equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr and (2) the Al-modified variant with ~5 at.% aluminum substituted into the alloy. Subject both sets to isothermal air exposure for 5 hours at a temperature within the 800–1000 °C range. Post-exposure, carry out cross-sectional microstructural analyses (using SEM/EDS) to assess the integrity and thickness of the formed oxide scales, and perform weight-gain measurements to quantify oxidation. Additionally, conduct tensile tests at room temperature and high temperature (1000 °C) to compare mechanical performance.
measurements: Oxide scale thickness and continuity (via SEM/EDS)
Room temperature tensile properties (ductility, ultimate tensile strength)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-modified alloy does not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in oxidation (i.e., lower weight gain and thinner, more adherent oxide scale) and if its mechanical properties deviate by more than ±10% from those of the baseline alloy under the test conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

Abstract: AbstractCoating system(s) will be required for Nb-silicide based alloys. Alumina forming alloys that are chemically compatible with the Nb-silicide based alloy substrate could be components of such systems. A Study of the Effect of 5 at.% Sn on the Micro-Structure and Isothermal Oxidation at 800 and 1200 °C of Nb-24Ti-18Si Based Alloys with Al and/or Cr Additions

Abstract: AbstractThis paper presents the results of a systematic study of Nb-24Ti-18Si based alloys with 5 at.% Sn addition. Three alloys of nominal compositions (at.%), namely Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Cr-5Sn (ZX4), Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Al-5Sn (ZX6), and Nb-24Ti-18Si-5Al-5Cr-5Sn (ZX8), were studied to understand how the increased Sn concentration improved oxidation resistance. In all three alloys there was macrosegregation, which was most severe in ZX8 and the primary βNb5Si3 transformed completely to αNb5Si3 after heat treatment. The Nbss was not stable in ZX6, the Nb3Sn was stable in all three alloys, and the Nbss and C14-NbCr2 Laves phase were stable in ZX4 and ZX8. The 5 at.% Sn addition suppressed pest oxidation at 800 °C but not scale spallation at 1200 °C. At both temperatures, a Sn-rich area with Nb3Sn, Nb5Sn2Si, and NbSn2 compounds developed below the scale.
